paths.title: Rudder Park's 'Problem Was Resolved'/'Was Managed' — An Outcome Claim Beyond What This Case's Own Record Establishes
analysis: Two of this case's own operator-supplied documents assert an outcome for Rudder Park that this case uses as its central comparator for what a Bellbrook plan could achieve. The Facts Insert states: 'Kempsey Shire Council has a completed management plan for one site: Rudder Park in East Kempsey. That plan was completed in 2022. East Kempsey's problem was resolved with the help of that plan.' The Media Pitch states, of the same site: 'Kempsey Shire Council's only completed plan is for Rudder Park, East Kempsey — completed 2022. East Kempsey's problem was managed. Bellbrook's was not.'

This case's own most methodologically careful primary source, the Community Harm and Accountability Record (SRC-0007), describes the same fact more narrowly: 'Vegetation management at that site was completed in July 2022' - a description of a specific management action's completion, not a statement that the underlying community-harm 'problem' was thereby resolved or managed as an outcome. This case's evidence register captures the same narrower claim: EV-0002's own relevant_quotation reads only 'That plan was completed in 2022,' stopping before the Facts Insert's own next sentence about the problem being 'resolved'. No document or evidence item anchored anywhere in this case states, or corroborates, that Rudder Park's underlying flying-fox impacts - as distinct from the vegetation-management action itself - reached any confirmed outcome.

Checked against source_register.json in full before writing this path: SRC-0005's own entry records only that the Facts Insert 'States Rudder Park's management plan was "completed in 2022"' and SRC-0010's own entry records only its distinct 'historic' classification claim (already the subject of AR-016/CTR-0002) - neither entry notes this outcome-overstatement, so this is a genuinely new finding, not a re-litigation.
determinations: The claim that Rudder Park's 'problem was resolved'/'was managed' - used in this case's own advocacy material to argue that a Bellbrook plan would produce a genuine outcome, not merely process activity - is not established anywhere in this case's own primary source record. The only confirmed fact is that a vegetation-management action was completed there in 2022. This is the same documented-activity-versus-confirmed-outcome distinction this case's own findings already apply rigorously to Bellbrook's own advocacy record (AR-011; the Harm and Accountability Record's own Finding 5) - here it surfaces, for the first time, in how this case's own material describes the comparator site it relies on to make that same argument for Bellbrook.
paths.boundary: Does not determine that Rudder Park's underlying flying-fox impacts were NOT resolved or managed - only that no document or evidence item in this case's own record confirms an outcome beyond the vegetation-management action's completion; the comparator site's real-world outcome may in fact be positive, and this path does not rule that out. Does not allege deliberate overstatement - 'resolved' and 'managed' may reflect a genuine but uncorroborated belief on the drafters' part, the same innocent-explanation caution this case already applies to every other instance of this pattern (CPO-010). The Media Pitch's own 'managed' phrasing is not itself the subject of a dedicated evidence item in this case's register - EV-0009, the only item sourced to that document, concerns a distinct claim (the 'historic' classification) - so this path anchors only to EV-0002, the item that does capture the underlying Rudder Park completion fact both documents build on. Does not propose contacting anyone or correcting either document (see DEC-0008).

paths.title: The Harm and Accountability Record's Own 2021 Timeline Entry — Never Checked Against This Case's Independently-Found 2021 Departure Record
analysis: The Community Harm and Accountability Record's own governance timeline (Section 3) contains an entry, filed under its '2022' year-heading rather than the '2020–2021' heading immediately above it, reading in full: '2021: Kempsey Shire Council publishes a council news item acknowledging flying-foxes at Bellbrook. paths.boundary: Does not determine whether SRC-0007's 2021 entry and EV-0013/SRC-0012 describe the same council communication or two separate ones - SRC-0007's own account is too terse ('institutional acknowledgement') to identify the specific item it refers to, and this case has not independently sighted whichever item it is. paths.title: AR-053's Own Comparator Source Uses 'Management Outcome' Language Too - In a Section AR-053 Did Not Check, and in a Third Document AR-053 Did Not Examine

paths.title: AR-028's 'No Response From DCCEEW' Silence Item - Checked Against the One DCCEEW Reply This Case's Own Record Already Holds

paths.title: The Hardened Submission Package's Own Population-Increase Claim — Self-Flagged as Unquantified, Consistent With This Case's Own 'No Assessment Ever Conducted' Finding

paths.title: The Media Pitch's Own 'Key Facts' Section Independently Restates Four Already-Anchored Facts, None of Which Credit It as a Corroborating Source

paths.title: A Fifth Report-Back-Absence Cycle — the Harm and Accountability Record's Own 17 March 2026 Timeline Entry, From a Second Document AR-010 Did Not Check
analysis: AR-009 establishes that the October 2025 absence of any Bellbrook flying-fox item is cross-source confirmed. AR-010 establishes that the Hardened Submission Package's own extension of that absence to the November 2025, December 2025 and February 2026 meeting cycles is a single-source claim, carried only by that one document (SRC-0006) and not independently cross-checked by any other document in this case. No prior path has examined the Community Harm and Accountability Record's own governance timeline (Section 3) for a comparable entry of its own. It contains one, dated after the four months AR-009/AR-010 already treat: '17 March 2026: Ordinary council meeting. No motion, amendment, or statement on Bellbrook flying fox management recorded in the confirmed minutes.'

This is a fifth reporting-cycle absence, and the first to come from a second, independently-purposed document (SRC-0007) rather than only the Hardened Submission Package AR-010 already treats with caution. But the apparent independence is weaker than it looks: SRC-0007 states its own 'Evidence Base' as drawing on 'Kempsey Shire Council confirmed minutes 2022-2026' - the same claimed evidentiary basis AR-037 already found this investigation has never itself independently obtained through any channel available to it, Council's own site and web.archive.org having both blocked automated fetch attempts. The 17 March 2026 entry rests on that same unverified basis, like every other minutes-derived claim in this document's own timeline.

Checked against source_register.json in full before writing this path: SRC-0007's own entry does not record this specific March entry or connect it to AR-009/AR-010's existing absence pattern, and evidence_register.json's own EV-0005 entry - which already credits SRC-0007 for the cross-source-confirmed October absence specifically - credits only SRC-0006 for the extension beyond October, with no mention of a March 2026 entry at all. Neither record draws this connection, so this is a genuinely new finding, not a re-litigation.
determinations: The report-back-absence pattern this case already documents for four consecutive cycles extends to a fifth, 17 March 2026, and for the first time from a document other than the Hardened Submission Package - but this does not strengthen AR-010's own single-source caution about the extended months the way genuine cross-corroboration would. The document supplying this fifth month claims its own basis is 'confirmed minutes' this investigation has never independently obtained (AR-037), so the new entry carries that same unverified-basis caution rather than resolving it.
paths.boundary: Does not treat this as independent cross-source corroboration of the same months AR-010 already flags as uncorroborated - SRC-0007 and SRC-0006 describe different calendar months, not the same one twice, so this extends the documented absence pattern rather than confirming an existing instance of it. Does not determine whether SRC-0007's minutes-based claims are accurate - only that they carry the same caution AR-037 already established for this document's self-described evidentiary basis. Does not modify evidence_register.json's EV-0005 entry or chronology.json - both are DFAPTI-level frozen files this DFAPTA pass does not edit; recommends a future DFAPTI pass add this entry to EV-0005's corroboration list or mint a dedicated evidence item for it. Does not allege EV-0005's existing entry was drafted carelessly - a plausible innocent explanation is that it was written before this specific line of SRC-0007's own governance timeline had been checked against it, the same category of completeness gap AR-058 already found and did not attribute to carelessness.

paths.title: Two Ombudsman Act Complaints in This Case's Own Material, Never Compared - the More Severe Characterisation Rests on the Less Corroborated Claim
analysis: This case's preserved material contains two separately-drafted complaints to the NSW Ombudsman under the Ombudsman Act 1974 (NSW), addressing overlapping Kempsey Shire Council conduct. The Hardened Submission Package's Part 5 ('Submission 2: NSW Ombudsman') states its own Statutory Issue as: council's public characterisation of Resolution 2025.80's passage as active engagement, followed by non-disclosure of the missed October report-back milestone, 'constitutes systemic maladministration and misleading public notification under the Ombudsman Act 1974.' Its own Matters of Fact rest specifically on 'Resolution 2025.80 passed 9/0 on 20 May 2025' - the same numbered-resolution claim AR-006 already establishes as this case's most specific and least corroborated account of the May 2025 meeting, mentioned by no other document and unconfirmed against the signed minutes (CTR-0001, Q-0001).

The standalone Ombudsman Complaint (EV-0007), drafted separately and, per source_register.json's own SRC-0006 entry, following the Hardened Submission Package as a later document in this case's own drafting sequence, asks the Ombudsman only to investigate whether council's conduct 'constitutes unreasonable, unjust, or otherwise defective conduct under the Ombudsman Act 1974' - a materially less severe characterisation that does not use the word 'maladministration' anywhere in its own text. Its own four numbered matters of conduct (the October agenda omission, non-disclosure of the August/September 2025 consultation's outputs, the plan-gated grants disparity AR-048 already treats, and the unexplained silence on the May 2025 decision) rest instead on the SRC-0001-consistent account of the meeting - the account every independently-fetched source in this case corroborates - and do not cite any resolution number or vote count at all.

No prior path anchors both EV-0007 and EV-0010 together or reads the two documents' own Ombudsman submissions side by side. AR-006 examines EV-0010's resolution claim in isolation from this case's advocacy material; AR-048 examines EV-0007's equity framing in isolation from the Hardened Submission Package's own, differently-targeted Ombudsman submission. Checked against source_register.json in full before writing this path: SRC-0006's own entry notes generally that this document 'reads as an earlier, more aggressive draft than the harm/accountability record and formal complaint letters that followed it,' but does not itself identify that both documents draft a complaint to the same statutory recipient under the same Act, or that the earlier document's complaint is the one built on this case's single least-corroborated factual claim; SRC-0011's own entry records only that this document's meeting account matches SRC-0001 and that it carries this case's most detailed chronology, with no cross-reference to the Hardened Submission Package's own Ombudsman submission. Neither entry draws this specific connection, so this is a genuinely new finding, not a re-litigation.
determinations: The single most legally severe characterisation of council's conduct anywhere in this case's material ('systemic maladministration and misleading public notification') is the one built on this case's single least-corroborated specific factual claim (the 9/0 Resolution 2025.80 vote); this case's own later, better-corroborated complaint draft to the identical statutory recipient under the identical Act uses a markedly less severe characterisation and does not rely on the uncorroborated resolution numbers at all. This extends source_register.json's own general 'earlier, more aggressive draft' observation about SRC-0006 into a specific, directly comparable pair of documents addressed to the same external body.
paths.boundary: Does not determine which document's characterisation of council's conduct, if either, the NSW Ombudsman would find accurate - that determination is outside this investigation's authority, and this path does not adopt 'systemic maladministration' or 'unreasonable, unjust, or otherwise defective conduct' as its own finding; it records only that the two characterisations exist in this case's own material and differ in severity in a way tied to the underlying claim's own corroboration level. Does not allege the later, less severe draft reflects a deliberate correction of the earlier one - a plausible innocent explanation is that the two documents were drafted for different purposes or by different methods, and that specific claims proved harder to sustain once corroboration was attempted, consistent with the general pattern SRC-0006's own source_register entry already notes without this specific comparison. Does not propose lodging either complaint, naming any additional recipient, or adopting any remedy sought by either document's own relief-seeking language, including the Hardened Submission Package's own Improvement Notice and audit requests (see DEC-0008) - it records only that both documents exist in the source material and target the same statutory recipient. Does not extend to the Hardened Submission Package's other two Part 5 submissions (Office of Local Government NSW, SafeWork NSW), which AR-006 already references as resting on the same uncorroborated resolution claim without a comparably-targeted second document to compare them against.

cross_path_observations.title: The plan mechanism is demonstrated, not exotic
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-001, AR-003 and AR-004 converge: the management-plan instrument is actively operated inside Kempsey Shire itself (Rudder Park), actively revised by a comparable regional council (Townsville), and specifically funded for development elsewhere (Mount Isa). No single path alone shows all three; together they remove 'this is a rare or unfunded mechanism' as an available explanation for Bellbrook's absence of one.

cross_path_observations.title: Three accounts, three different evidentiary weights
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-005, AR-006, AR-007 and AR-008 together show the meeting-account dispute is not a simple two-sided contradiction - it is three accounts with three distinct sourcing profiles, only one of which (AR-006) supplies the specific numbers this case's strongest remedy language would need, and that one is also the least corroborated.

cross_path_observations.title: The report-back gap has a confirmed core and an unconfirmed extension
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-009 and AR-010 together show this case should not treat 'no report-back through February 2026' as a single fact of uniform confidence - the October 2025 absence is cross-source confirmed; the extension through November, December and February is currently single-source, carried only by the Hardened Submission Package. AR-059 adds a further complication rather than resolving it: the Harm and Accountability Record's own governance timeline independently extends the absence to a fifth month, 17 March 2026, from a second document - but that document's own claimed evidentiary basis ('confirmed minutes 2022-2026') is exactly what AR-037 already found this investigation has never itself independently obtained, so this apparent second-source status should not be read as stronger corroboration than AR-010's own single-source caution already applies.

cross_path_observations.title: One Commonwealth channel, two distinct open questions
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-013, AR-014 and AR-015 together show the Commonwealth registration attempt produced one hard confirmed fact (the program's pause) and left one genuinely separate question open (the EPBC threshold) - these should not be treated as a single resolved 'Commonwealth pathway is dead' finding.

cross_path_observations.title: Three independent strands, no single conclusive one
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-016, AR-017 and AR-018 each bear on whether Bellbrook's camp is accurately described as 'historic' - a partially-corroborated classification claim, an unlocated severity report, and a confirmed real 2021 departure that could fully explain the classification without inaccuracy. No single strand is conclusive; read together they show why CTR-0002 remains genuinely, not just formally, open.

cross_path_observations.title: Two health mechanisms, not one 'health risk' finding
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-019 and AR-020 are structurally distinct risks (fungal, droppings-borne vs. viral, bite/scratch-borne) that a less granular pass would have compressed into a single generic 'health risk exists' path - keeping them separate preserves the different evidentiary bases each actually has.

cross_path_observations.title: One confirmed action stands apart from four unconfirmed drafts
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-013 and AR-021 together show this case's advocacy record is not a uniform set of 'things the operator tried' - one action (Commonwealth registration) has a confirmed send date and a confirmed reply; four drafted channels (council, Ombudsman, and two more referenced in the same drafting round) remain unconfirmed. Conflating them would overstate what has actually been attempted - and AR-034 shows one source document actively asserts they were sent while the drafts themselves show no sign of it.

cross_path_observations.title: Primary-source re-reading surfaces what register summaries compress away
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-024 through AR-036 exist only because Pass 2 went back to the eight preserved primary documents directly rather than relying on evidence_register.json's own condensed descriptions. The most significant single finding of this pass - AR-034's lodgement-status contradiction - was invisible in Pass 1 precisely because the register's EV-0006/EV-0007 summaries describe the drafts' content, not the tension between the media pitch's completion claim and the drafts' own unsigned state. The three-way colony-continuity discrepancy (AR-024) is the same pattern: a real inconsistency that exists in the frozen source material regardless of which pass reads it, but that only a close primary-source read surfaces.

cross_path_observations.title: The case's most specific detail and its most cautious sourcing share one document
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-006 (the specific resolution numbers), AR-025 (the defeated Rudder Park absorption amendment), AR-031 (the self-excluded canopy-degradation section) and AR-032's most specific detail (the 30-metre buffer figure) all originate in the single least-corroborated document in this case, the Hardened Submission Package. This is not a reason to discount them individually - each stands or falls on its own terms - but the concentration is itself worth naming: this case's most granular procedural and technical detail and its most evidentially cautious material are the same document.

cross_path_observations.title: The claims-vs-record gap pattern recurs a seventh time
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-006 (the Hardened Submission Package's specific resolution numbers, uncorroborated elsewhere), AR-034 (the media pitch's 'have now been lodged' claim against the drafts' own unsigned state), AR-037 (two documents' own 'confirmed minutes' claims against this case's inability to obtain them through any channel), AR-049 (the Greens senator letter's claim that 'the state minister has received correspondence,' a state-level action no other document in this case corroborates in those terms), AR-050 (the Hardened Submission Package's claim that council's own public communications 'characterised the resolution as evidence of active council engagement,' checked against this case's own independently-sourced meeting-wrap content, which frames the same motion more narrowly), AR-051 (the Hardened Submission Package's specifically-attributed claim, and the Harm and Accountability Record's vaguer inference, that council itself communicated a 'legal protection means no action is possible' framing - neither corroborated by this case's one directly-preserved council communication, EV-0004, or any independently-fetched council source), AR-053 (the Facts Insert's and Media Pitch's claim that Rudder Park's 'problem was resolved'/'was managed', checked against this case's own more careful primary source, which states only that a vegetation-management action was completed there), and AR-055 (the same careful primary source's own governance timeline, and the Ombudsman complaint's chronology, both independently using 'management outcome' language for the same Rudder Park fact - a broader framing than the same source's Section 4 language AR-053 itself relied on) are eight separate instances of the same underlying pattern: a document in this case's own source material asserting a more complete or more certain state of affairs than this case's independently-verifiable record supports. No single instance establishes bad faith or error on its own - each has its own boundary and a plausible innocent explanation this analysis does not rule out - but the recurrence across eight distinct documents and claims is itself worth naming as a pattern future passes on this case should watch for. AR-050 is the first instance checked against this case's own independently-fetched material (EV-0003) rather than only against an absence of corroboration; AR-051 is the first instance concerning an alleged council statement or communication practice rather than a specific number, date, or characterisation of a documented action; AR-053 is the first instance concerning a claim about the comparator site (Rudder Park) rather than about Bellbrook's own record or advocacy chain; AR-055 is the first instance to recur inside this case's own most methodologically careful primary source itself, rather than only in the persuasive-drafting or advocacy material.

cross_path_observations.title: The Level 1/2 finding has an unresolved framing tension underneath it
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-012 and AR-032 treat Level 1/Level 2 management actions as available to council independent of a Camp Management Plan - the basis for AR-012's determination that legal species-protection does not by itself explain the absence of interim action at Bellbrook. AR-039 shows the same primary source material also contains, in the same document and in the same section that most authoritatively states the Plan's role, a description of the Plan itself as the authorising 'gateway' for those same Level 1/2 actions - a framing AR-012 and AR-032 do not currently carry, and which would complicate their determination if accurate. This does not overturn AR-012 or AR-032 - it names an unresolved tension between two readings of the same case material that only surfaces when different sections of the same document are read against each other, and that the primary Code of Practice text (DR-004) is needed to resolve.

cross_path_observations.title: The 'lodged' claim fails on two independent grounds, not one
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-034 shows the documents that would need to be lodged remain unsigned templates. AR-045 shows that, setting signature status aside, this case's material contains a matching drafted document for only two of the six recipients the claim names. Read together, the six-recipient 'simultaneously lodged' claim in the media pitch and the council-submission letter is unsupported by this case's own document set on two independent grounds - lowering, rather than raising, confidence that Q-0005 will resolve toward 'already sent'.

cross_path_observations.title: Four lenses on the same Rudder Park/Bellbrook gap, none of them conclusive
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-001, AR-038, AR-048 and AR-053 each bear on the same underlying fact - Rudder Park has a completed plan, Bellbrook does not - from four different angles that this case should not collapse into one. AR-001 shows council capability: the instrument is not unfamiliar. AR-038 shows a single-source, uncorroborated claim of an actual 2022 assessment that could, if accurate, function as a justification. AR-048 shows one of this case's own drafted advocacy documents frames the outcome as unequal treatment absent adequate justification - a framing that does not engage with, or rule out, AR-038's possible justification. AR-053 goes a step earlier than any of the other three: it questions whether the comparator's own success - the premise all three other lenses treat as given - is itself established by this case's record, finding that it is not, beyond the vegetation-management action's completion. None of the four resolves the question the others leave open; together they show why this case's own material does not yet support a conclusion either way on why the two sites diverged, and why even the benchmark used to frame that question rests on less than the advocacy material assumes.

cross_path_observations.title: Three unobtained primary documents, only two ever requested
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-002 (the grants program's own guidelines, DR-003/Q-0002), AR-039 (the Code of Practice 2018's primary text, DR-004/Q-0007) and AR-052 (the Policy 2015, newly named at DR-005) each identify a distinct primary regulatory or programmatic document this case's central Camp Management Plan finding depends on but has never obtained. Read together, they show this case's own disclosure-request register was, until this pass, missing a target for the specific instrument its own most careful primary source (SRC-0007) credits with establishing the mechanism in the first place - not because the gap was deliberately left out, but because AR-002 and AR-039 each named the document nearest to their own specific question (the grants program's eligibility rule; the Code of Practice's Level 1/2 operational detail) without separately naming the Policy that Section 4 and Section 7 attribute the broader authorising and gating role to.

cross_path_observations.title: The document that argues hardest also flags its own gaps three times
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-031 (Part 3's canopy-degradation mechanism, self-limited to 'comparable managed sites' absent Bellbrook-specific survey data), AR-035 (Part 6's three evidence-collection matrices, proposing future data the document does not yet have) and AR-057 (Part 1.1's population-increase claim, self-flagged as needing 'Tier 1-2' quantified data) are three separate, textually distinct instances - spanning the document's historical, ecological, and forward-planning sections - of the same single document explicitly acknowledging, in its own words, that a claim it makes or an argument it advances currently lacks the evidentiary basis to be treated as confirmed. Read together with CPO-009 (which already names this document, the Hardened Submission Package, as the source of both this case's most specific procedural detail and its most cautious sourcing), this shows the document's acknowledgment of its own evidentiary limits is not an isolated hedge but a recurring structural feature of it.

cross_path_observations.title: The Media Pitch is corroboration this case's own register doesn't credit
cross_path_observations.analysis: AR-040 (the November 2019 bushfire-origin claim, currently unanchored by any dedicated evidence item) and AR-058 (four further facts, each already anchored by an existing evidence item but without the Media Pitch listed among their corroborating sources) together show the same underlying gap recurring five times across this case's own register: the Media Pitch's own 'Key Facts' section independently restates nearly everything this case's material already establishes elsewhere, plus one genuinely novel claim (EV-0009's 'historic' classification, correctly and solely credited to it) - yet the register's own corroboration counts and citations do not reflect the document's actual role. No single instance changes any finding's substance; together they show a specific, narrow gap in citation completeness, distinct from CPO-010's opposite-direction pattern of source documents overstating their own evidentiary basis.

disclosure_requests.title: Signed confirmed minutes, 20 May 2025 Kempsey Shire Council ordinary meeting
disclosure_requests.request: The primary record needed to resolve CTR-0001 and Q-0001 - which of the three accounts (AR-005, AR-006, AR-007) is accurate, including whether Resolution 2025.79/2025.80 and the stated 9/0 vote and defeated 2/7 amendment are real.

disclosure_requests.request: A dated, directly-sighted capture of the page's full text - the 'historic' classification, the Rudder Park comparison, and the private/Crown land management claims - needed to resolve Q-0004, Q-0009 and CTR-0002.

disclosure_requests.title: NSW Government flying-fox camp management grants program guidelines
disclosure_requests.request: The program's own published eligibility terms, to confirm or correct the operator-supplied claim analysed in AR-002 that a completed or draft Camp Management Plan is a strict funding precondition. AR-041 (Pass 6) adds a further specific question this same guidance would resolve: whether the plan-gating rule applies to infrastructure-hardening grant categories (park shelters, bus stop shielding) the same way it applies to the vegetation-management grants EV-0011 was originally drawn from, or whether a separate, non-plan-gated funding route exists for hardening works.

disclosure_requests.request: To confirm the Level 1/Level 2 management actions described in AR-012 against the Code's actual text, including whether Level 1/Level 2 actions require a completed or draft Camp Management Plan as a prerequisite or are available regardless of one - the tension AR-039 identifies between different sections of this case's own source material.

disclosure_requests.request: To confirm the Community Harm and Accountability Record's own claim (Section 4, Section 7) that this Policy - a distinct instrument from the Code of Practice 2018 already requested at DR-004 - is what establishes the Camp Management Plan mechanism, its Level 1/2 authorisation role, and its grant-funding-eligibility rule (AR-002's Q-0002, AR-039's framing tension, AR-052). The Code of Practice appears from this case's own source material to supply only the itemised Level 1/2 operational detail (AR-032), while the Policy is what the source material itself credits with the plan-gating and authorisation rule.

contradictions_preserved.issue: Three distinct accounts of the 20 May 2025 council meeting remain in tension - see AR-005 through AR-008 for the full triangulation.
contradictions_preserved.analysis: Not resolved by this analysis - the signed confirmed minutes have not been obtained across seven runs and two case-creation passes.

contradictions_preserved.issue: Council's current 'historic' classification may or may not match a functional 2026 reality of severe, ongoing impact - see AR-016 through AR-018 for the three independent strands bearing on this, and AR-024 for a related, separate three-way discrepancy over when the colony was actually present.
contradictions_preserved.analysis: Not resolved by this analysis - the June 2026 report has not been located and it is not established whether the colony returned after its confirmed 2021 departure, or whether the Hardened Submission Package's uncited December 2019 start date and mid-2022 return describe the same event or a different history again.

overreach_controls: No claim is made about why Kempsey Shire Council has not produced a Bellbrook-specific management plan - only that it has not, against a mechanism it operates elsewhere in the same shire.
No intent is attributed to any individual councillor, council officer, or Commonwealth official at any point in this analysis - every finding describes documented institutional record, not motive.

AR-006 and AR-008 do not adopt the Hardened Submission Package's characterisation of council's conduct as non-execution of an affirmative unanimous directive - that characterisation depends on the unresolved CTR-0001 and is not treated as established here.

AR-016 through AR-018 do not present the 'historic' classification as inaccurate or as a confirmed documented-vs-functional gap - CTR-0002 remains genuinely open, with a real alternative explanation (the 2021 departure, AR-018) not yet ruled out.

AR-019 and AR-020 do not claim any Bellbrook resident has experienced histoplasmosis or an ABLV exposure - both are stated as real mechanisms without a confirmed local instance, matching the source evidence's own explicit hedge.

AR-031 and AR-032 do not adopt the 30-metre buffer figure or any other Hardened Submission Package detail as confirmed - both originate in the least-corroborated document in this case (see CPO-009) and are presented as candidate material, not established findings.

AR-031 explicitly excludes the Hardened Submission Package's canopy-degradation section from this case's evidentiary basis, matching that section's own self-declared limitation - it is documented here as existing in the source material, not relied upon.

AR-024 and AR-034 name real inconsistencies in this case's own frozen source material without resolving them or assuming which side of each is accurate - resolving them is a DFAPTI-level task (confirming facts, obtaining the operator's clarification) that this DFAPTA pass does not perform. A third apparent inconsistency (originally AR-023, an advocate named 'Paul Hodgson' in five documents and 'Paul Hodgkinson' in one) was removed 2026-08-25 (DEC-0009) - this is a single-document spelling variant, not a genuine unresolved discrepancy, and treating it as one overstated a trivial transcription artefact as material uncertainty. Correct verification practice recognises and normalises an obvious variant against five consistent references rather than preserving it as an open question.

This analysis does not propose remedies, recipients, or submission strategies for any finding - a SafeWork NSW/Work Health and Safety Act theory and an Office of Local Government NSW submission pathway (originally AR-029, AR-030) and a sixth advocacy channel to Senator Faruqi (originally AR-033) were removed 2026-08-25 after the operator flagged that Advocacy Package-only content - remedies sought, recipients, what to ask them for - had been run through the analysis gate (DEC-0008). DFAPTA states what the evidence and source material show; who to send it to and what to ask for belongs to Enforcement Notice and Advocacy Package, neither of which exists yet.

This pass deliberately does not compress distinct claims of different evidentiary weight into single generic findings (see AR-022, CPO-006, CPO-007 and CPO-008) - the original nine-path pass's central failure was doing exactly that, and is not repeated here.

AR-037 and CPO-010 do not allege any document's claims-vs-record gap was made in bad faith or deliberately - each has a plausible innocent explanation (loose use of 'confirmed', aspirational drafting, or a record-keeping oversight) that this analysis does not rule in or rule out. AR-038 does not allege council concealed a 2022 assessment - only that if the single source describing one is accurate, it was never disclosed to residents in any document this case has sighted.

AR-039 does not determine whether Level 1/Level 2 management actions genuinely require a Camp Management Plan as a legal prerequisite or are available regardless of one - it names a framing tension inside the case's own primary source material (including within a single document) that only the primary Code of Practice text itself (DR-004) can resolve, and does not treat either framing as established over the other.

AR-040 does not allege chronology.json's CHR-0001 citation was corrupted or altered - only that it currently references an evidence item whose own description concerns a different event, a gap this pass identifies but does not correct, since chronology.json is a DFAPTI-level frozen file this analysis does not modify.

AR-041 does not determine whether council has, or lacks, any funding route for infrastructure hardening other than the plan-gated grants program - only that the one pathway this case's source material itself describes is plan-gated. It does not extend the Section 2 'available regardless' critique to resident subsidies or formal advocacy, which this path does not examine.

AR-042 does not allege DCCEEW, CSIRO or Kempsey Shire Council has concealed an existing assessment - it reports the operator's own sourced claim, made to DCCEEW directly, that no such assessment is known to have occurred, and does not treat that claim as independently confirmed.

AR-043 does not allege the August/September 2025 consultation's output was deliberately withheld or that no document chain exists - it reports that two draft advocacy documents characterise the absence that way, without adopting that characterisation as established, and does not propose that council be asked to produce the material or name any recipient for such a request (see DEC-0008).

AR-044 does not allege the May 2025 decision's non-reversal reflects deliberate obstruction, bad faith, or any other motive - it reports that two source documents state this as a governance-record fact, and does not treat 'not reversed in any confirmed record' as proof no internal reconsideration has occurred.

AR-045 does not allege submissions to the four unmatched recipients were never made, and does not allege the council-submission letter or media pitch overstated the six-recipient claim deliberately - it reports a document-coverage gap in this case's own preserved material, not a finding about what actually happened outside that material, and does not propose contacting any of the four unmatched recipients (see DEC-0008).

AR-046 does not determine which of the two dates (the record's own 'May 2026' or the three letters' 'June 2026') is accurate, and does not allege the mismatch was deliberate or that a substantively different document is at issue - it names a repeated citation discrepancy in this case's own preserved material, matching the same caution AR-024 and AR-034 apply to other internal inconsistencies, and does not propose any correction or recipient action (see DEC-0008).

AR-047 does not establish that camp monitoring data was withheld deliberately or at all, and does not allege the March 2026 letter's silence on this item is misleading - it names an item this analysis itself infers is uncovered by comparing one part of a source document against another, not an explicit third-party claim like AR-028 or AR-043, and this path's own boundary states that weaker evidentiary basis explicitly. It does not propose that residents be given the data or name any recipient for such a request (see DEC-0008).

AR-048 does not conclude that council's treatment of Bellbrook relative to Rudder Park was in fact unjustified or discriminatory - it reports that one of this case's own drafted advocacy documents frames the outcome that way, without adopting that characterisation, and does not resolve the tension with AR-038's possible-justification claim (see CPO-013). It does not adopt the Ombudsman complaint's own relief-seeking language and does not propose any remedy or name any recipient beyond the complaint's own already-drafted addressee (see DEC-0008).

AR-049 does not determine whether 'the state minister' is a loose reference to Michael Kemp MP or an independent, uncorroborated claim about the NSW Minister for Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water - it names a claims-vs-record gap in this case's own source material without resolving which reading is correct, does not allege the imprecision was deliberate, and does not propose contacting any recipient (see DEC-0008).

AR-050 does not establish that EV-0003 is the specific public communication the Hardened Submission Package's Part 2.2 refers to, and does not adopt that document's own Part 5 Ombudsman submission content built on the same claim (see DEC-0008) - it checks one factual claim against this case's own independently-sourced material and does not allege the characterisation was deliberately inaccurate.
